extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing Review articles for submission to F1000Research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting Review-type manuscripts to F1000Research, covering suitability, required sections, formatting, ethical disclosures, and the post-publication, author-led peer-review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Article suitability / Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome Review Articles that provide a balanced and comprehensive overview of the latest discoveries in a particular field and summarize topics that have not yet been covered in the same way in the existing published literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be based on peer-reviewed literature, and should not include new research, data or propose new hypotheses. The decision on whether a Review Article is suitable for publication and subsequent peer review ultimately lies with the Publishing Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles must be written in good English. Both UK English and US English are accepted but this must be consistent throughout the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article will not undergo editing by F1000Research before publication and a manuscript could be rejected during the initial checking process if it is deemed unintelligible and unsuitable for peer review. For authors whose first language is not English, it may be beneficial to have the manuscript read by a native English speaker with scientific expertise. Commercial editing services are available at author cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main sections / required components
rubrics_metrics.description: The article should include the following main sections: Authors, Title, Abstract, Keywords, Main Body, Data and Software Availability, Author Contributions, Competing Interests, Grant Information, Acknowledgments, References and footnotes, Figures and Tables, Units, Symbols and Mathematical Scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The format of the main body is flexible and should be appropriate for the review; ensure all statements are supported by appropriate and up-to-date references. Do not include unpublished research and datasets in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors should have made a significant contribution to the work and agree to be accountable for the parts of the work they have done. All authors should approve the final version for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being an author implies full responsibility for the article’s content and that the work conforms to editorial policies. For large, multi-centre collaborations, individuals who accept direct responsibility for the manuscript must be listed as authors. Details of each author’s contribution must be listed in the Author contributions section. Anyone who contributed but does not meet authorship criteria should be listed in Acknowledgments. The involvement of any professional medical writer assistance must be declared. See ICMJE Uniform Requirements for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise and specific title that clearly reflects the content of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts should be up to 300 words long and provide a succinct summary of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should explain why the article might be interesting but should not over-emphasize the importance of the work. Citations should not be used in the abstract. Abbreviations, if needed, should be spelled out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should supply up to eight relevant keywords that describe the subject of their article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords will improve the visibility of your article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main body content and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The main body should be concise, easy to read and presented in a format appropriate for the type of review. Ensure that all statements are supported by appropriate and up-to-date references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include unpublished research and datasets in your review (these belong in Research articles, Research Notes, or other article types). For most Reviews the recommended format is: Introduction; Discussion/analysis of the recent literature; Conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Software Availability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles must include a Data Availability Statement, even where there is no data associated with the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Review-type articles (which should not include new research/data) the Data Availability Statement should read: 'No data are associated with this article.' See the data guidelines and policies for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions (CRediT Taxonomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research uses the CRediT Taxonomy to capture author contributions to bring transparency and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to include an Author Contributions section in your manuscript: on submission you will be asked for the contributions made by each author, to be selected from the CRediT list (Conceptualization, Data Curation, Formal Analysis, Funding Acquisition, Investigation, Methodology, Project Administration, Resources, Software, Supervision, Validation, Visualization, Writing – Original Draft Preparation, Writing – Review & Editing, etc.). Anyone who contributed but does not meet authorship criteria should appear in Acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing Interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must include a Competing Interests section disclosing any financial, personal, or professional competing interests that could unduly influence the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing Interests will be displayed alongside the article. Articles must not contain content that could be perceived as 'advertising'. If there are no competing interests, add the text 'No competing interests were disclosed'. More examples are in editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant information
rubrics_metrics.description: State who funded the work, whether it is your employer, a grant funder etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not list funding that is not relevant to this specific piece of research. For each funder state the funder’s name, the grant number where applicable, and the individual to whom the grant was assigned. If no grants funded the work, include a 'Grant information' section and state: 'The author(s) declared that no grants were involved in supporting this work'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge anyone who contributed to the research or writing but does not qualify as an author, and clearly state how they contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permission to include the name and affiliation of anyone mentioned. Grant funding should not be listed in Acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and footnotes formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: References and footnotes can be listed in any standard style if it is consistent within the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations and journal names should align with discipline-specific standards. Preprints can be cited and listed. Unpublished abstracts, papers submitted but not accepted, and personal communications should be included in the text as 'personal communications' or 'unpublished work' and the named researchers, and authors are responsible for permission to quote. Web links should be included as hyperlinks within the main body, not as references. Datasets published/deposited elsewhere should be listed in the References section and follow provided citation examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and Tables — citation, number and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures and tables should be cited and discussed in the article text. There is no limit to the number of figures and tables you can have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure legends and tables should be added at the end of the manuscript. Tables should be formatted using the 'Insert Table' function in Word or provided as an Excel file. For larger tables/spreadsheets see the data guidelines. Files for figures are usually best uploaded as separate files through the submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and Tables — titles, legends and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure or table should have a concise title of no more than 15 words and a legend that briefly describes key points and explains symbols and abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legend should be sufficiently detailed so the figure or table can stand alone. If reusing a figure/table from previous publication, authors are responsible for obtaining permission and paying fees. Include a permission note in the legend stating reproduction with permission and original citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and Tables — file formats and technical image requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred colour mode: RGB or grayscale. Line art, photographs, mixed images and images used as data have specific format and resolution requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line art: text at least 8pt, lines thick enough to be seen at display size, consistent font, white background. Graphs: export as EPS file or provide original file (e.g., Excel). Other line art: EPS or original source (EPS/AI or DOC/DOCX/PPT/PPTX). If not possible accept uncompressed TIFFs at ≥600 dpi for line art. Photographs/microscopy: uncompressed TIFFs at ≥300 dpi. Mixed images (half-tone + line art): TIFF at 500 dpi or vector files. Images used as data: submit as uncompressed TIFF files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image manipulation and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic manipulation of images is allowed only to improve clarity and must be done transparently without misrepresenting the data; original, unaltered source data must be provided with the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brightness, contrast or colour balance may be used but applied to the whole image; any non-linear adjustments must be made explicit in the figure legend. Specific features must not be added, amplified, removed or obscured. If figures are composed from images from different sources or parts, this must be made clear (e.g., adding dividing lines). Authors are required to include details of all modifications made to images in the Methods section, including the name and version number of the software used. See Policies on Image Manipulation for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, symbols and mathematical scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistency and clarity with mathematical symbols, units and scripts throughout the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care with subscripts/superscripts and differentiation between similar looking characters (ell vs one; oh vs zero). Scalar variables in italics, non-variable matter upright. Solidus '/' for simple fractions in text; exceptions apply. Solidus generally not used for units (use m s⁻¹ not m/s) unless convention dictates. Displayed equations referred to in text should be numbered serially on the right-hand side. Preferred styles: roman bold sans serif for tensors, bold serif italic for vectors, roman bold serif for matrices, medium-weight italic serif for scalar variables. Use roman 'd' for differentials. Braces/brackets order: {[( )] } except where mathematical convention dictates otherwise. Use SI units and provide conversions where relevant. For special characters/accents use recommended fonts and Unicode; submit Unicode fonts with the article if used. Specific guidance provided for transliterated Arabic (fonts and Unicode codes for ayn/hamza). Key principle: ensure consistency throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' role in the peer review process (author-led post-publication review)
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research operates a post-publication peer-review model where peer review happens after the article is published and the process is author-led.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide at least 5 reviewer suggestions suitable according to the Reviewer Criteria before the article can be published. After publication, authors are expected to continue providing reviewer suggestions until the article receives two peer review reports — the editorial team will contact authors when more reviewers are required. After two reports authors are strongly encouraged to revise the article according to reviewers' comments; reviewers can only re-review after a revised version is published. Once revised, original reviewers will be notified to re-review; authors may continue to provide reviewer suggestions while awaiting re-reviews.
